positive.query: How much should we spend on marketing next year to hit a $5M new revenue target, and how should we split it across channels?
Finance wants to cut our marketing budget by 20% next quarter. What should we cut first and what happens to pipeline?
Back-solve how many leads and opportunities we need by quarter from our revenue target and CRM conversion rates.

nearMiss.query: Write a one-page campaign plan for our spring product launch with goals, audience, message, and channels.
Build the full company operating budget for next year including engineering, G&A, and sales headcount.
Design a holdout test to prove whether our paid social ads cause incremental sales.

holdout.query: Our paid search CAC looks cheapest on average. Should we move more budget there, and how do we phase spend by quarter with a test reserve?

scenarios.task: Hypothetical inputs: new revenue target $1,200,000; average deal $20,000; opportunity-to-win rate 25%; lead-to-opportunity rate 10%; cost per lead $100; fixed marketing costs (people and tools) $360,000; 90-day sales cycle. Build the marketing budget, show the back-solve, and show what a 20% cut to the total does to programs and pipeline. The CEO also asks whether marketing should simply be a fixed percentage of revenue.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline quotes a typical percent-of-revenue benchmark as fact, spreads the budget evenly by quarter, and applies a 20% cut proportionally to every line including fixed costs.

scenarios.task: Hypothetical spend history. Channel A: $10,000 bought 50 customers, $20,000 bought 80, $30,000 bought 95. Channel B: $10,000 bought 30, $20,000 bought 55, $30,000 bought 75. The team plans to put $30,000 in A and $10,000 in B because A has the lower average CAC. Recommend how to allocate $40,000 and explain why.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline agrees with allocating by average CAC and does not compute the cost of the next customer in each channel.
